items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I heard Ray Charles sing “Hallelujah” before the record came out.

ctx.x: I love that. You know I do that now but I do it on a keyboard and only rarely do I get – someone will, every once in a while say like, “Where’s the bass coming from?” Or they’ll say, “Hey you play a pretty good bass for a keyboard player.” I like it. I think that in another life I was a bass player.

Well when I went to high school I couldn’t play accordion in band or orchestra so I started to play bass. And between playing bass and also playing accordion, it was an interesting start. At the age of 15, now this you’ll get a kick out of – at the age of 15 there was a place in Atlantic City that the older musicians were playing in. The kids were like 17, 18 years old. And they got another job in another place and they needed a band to go to Eddie’s Shamrock, which is on Kentucky Avenue. I was 15 going on 16, I…
All that like gets inside you I think, and later on you may not even remember where it came from but you use it.
